title: DX cohort retention ledger and initiative rotations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a lightweight, versioned "ledger" and rotation cadence to track DX initiatives (SDKs, docs, quickstarts) focused on cohort retention. The ledger centralizes initiative summaries, start/end dates, cohorts targeted, hypothesis, key signals, experiment variants, and handoff notes so PMs and SEs can run 6-week waves without losing institutional knowledge. The goal is repeatable, observable initiative rotations that measurably improve first-14-day retention for SDK adopters and quickstart users.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Ledger prototype with schema and UI view available in Confluence and CSV exportable; 2) Rotation cadence documented (6-week wave template) with checklist and handoff section; 3) Two pilot cohorts run (one SDK quickstart update, one docs-driven onboarding tweak) with retention measurement plan implemented and baseline vs week-2/week-14 signals captured; 4) Playbook reviewed and approved by DX leads and Eng enablement; 5) Observability links (segment/dashboard/GitHub PRs) referenced in all pilot rows.
measurement_plan: Primary metric: 14-day retention (SDK active tokens or API calls per org). Secondary: 7-day activation conversion, sample size per cohort, NPS/qualitative signals from forum/feedback form. Measurement artifacts: analytics dashboard (Amplitude), cohort tags in DB, PRs for quickstarts, and an automated weekly cohort snapshot job.
milestones: Pilot A: SDK quickstart experiment roll - 2026-03-03
Pilot B: Docs onboarding flow A/B - 2026-03-10
Collect and analyze cohort retention signals - 2026-03-24
risks: Inaccurate cohort tagging will produce noisy retention signals
Engineering capacity to instrument cohort events may delay pilots
Playbook adoption risk if format is too heavyweight for SEs/PMs
notes: Lean ledger preferred over monolithic tooling; start with Confluence + Google Sheet + CSV export and iterate toward a simple Airtable view if adoption warrants. Emphasize handoff notes and 'why' not just 'what' so future rotations can reuse learnings.
